clues.title: Plate: EU plate, coat of arms on red circle
text: Montenegro uses the standard European plate with a blue strip, and the Montenegro coat of arms on a **red circle**. The red circle is visible through the blur.
NOTE: The white section of Albanian licence plates do not have a red circle.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Standard European plate with a blue strip, but the coat of arms sits on a red circle that shows through the blur. Albanian plates have no red circle.

differs.how: Albanian plates have no red circle on the white part

clues.title: Google car: low Gen 4 'smallcam'
text: All Generation 4 coverage in Montenegro was taken using a “smallcam” camera, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.
NOTE: Most of the Balkans and southern Europe have Smallcam.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Gen 4 camera mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be fully see-through. Much of the Balkans and southern Europe has this.

clues.title: Landscape: small, mountainous, narrow roads
text: Montenegro is a small, **mountainous** country. Inland mountains are lush and green, while most coastal mountains have distinct exposed, light coloured rock. Most roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Inland mountains are lush and green, while coastal mountains show bare, light-coloured rock. Most roads are only one or two lanes wide.

clues.title: Bollard: black top, red reflector front
text: The most common bollard is white with a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back. The bollard also has a black top.
NOTE: These bollards are also found in Slovenia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White post with a black top, a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back. Slovenia uses the same bollard.

clues.title: Chevron: black on white or red on yellow
text: Montenegro uses **black on white** or **red on yellow** chevrons.
NOTE: Albania uses white on black chevrons.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Chevron signs are black on white, or red on yellow. Albania uses white on black instead.

differs.how: Albanian chevrons are white on black

clues.title: Guardrail: often rusty
text: Guardrails in Montenegro are often **rusted**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Guardrails are frequently rusty.

clues.title: Guardrail: both A-type and B-type
text: Montenegro is the only Balkan country where you’ll commonly see both [A-type](https://goo.gl/maps/fZCnn3jPH4By45ph7) and [B-type](https://goo.gl/maps/w9hnQsjxxJS2TbT1A) guardrails.
NOTE: For a good overview of European guardrails, see [this infographic](/images/montenegro/europeguardrail.png).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The only Balkan country where you commonly see both A-type and B-type guardrails, two different rail profiles, side by side.

clues.title: Pole: simple round concrete or wood
text: Montenegro uses simple **round concrete** or wooden poles.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Plain round concrete poles, or wooden ones.

clues.title: Google car: 'rifts' (stitching cracks), uncommon
text: ‘**Rifts**’ can uncommonly be seen in Montenegrin generation 3 coverage, due to poor stitching.
NOTE: Rifts are also common in Albania, and can rarely be seen in various other countries.

images.caption: Stitching cracks ('rifts') showing as dark smears in the sky

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Rifts are visible seams or cracks in the picture caused by poor stitching. They show up now and then in Gen 3 coverage. Albania has them often.

differs.how: Rifts are common in Albania, only occasional here

clues.title: Google car: short antenna by coast, long inland
text: Although rifts are common in generation 3 Montenegro coverage, coastal rounds **will almost never **have them. By the coast, there will be a [short antenna](https://goo.gl/maps/d7Fvp2NzZw37CxyFA) with no rifts. There will be a [long antenna](https://goo.gl/maps/Zpu6fUJ5o3LkTtxZ6) with rifts inland.
NOTE: An exception to this is the area around the coastal villages of Utjeha and Dobra Voda.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Rifts (stitching cracks) are common on Gen 3 inland, where the car has a long antenna. On the coast the car has a short antenna and almost never rifts, except near Utjeha and Dobra Voda.

clues.title: Landscape: green farm valleys, cleared hills
text: Green, **agricultural valleys** with deforested hills to make way for farmland are most commonly seen in the north.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north: green farming valleys with hills cleared of trees to make farmland.

clues.title: Landscape: touristy bay, swimwear, steep ridge
text: The Bay of Kotor has a **touristy and populated** feel to it, with many people dressed in swimwear. A distinct [steep, rocky ridge](https://goo.gl/maps/Sj5ENoJMcprLyLzWA) can also be seen.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A busy, touristy bay with many people in swimwear and a steep rocky ridge above it.

clues.title: Landscape: dry treeless mountains, vineyards
text: **Dry mountains** with a lack of trees are seen around Podgorica, and to the south of it. Vineyards are also commonly seen in this region.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Around the capital and south of it: dry, treeless mountains, with vineyards common.

clues.title: Landscape: pine forests, mostly east
text: **Pine forests** can be found in the north and a small area north of Nikšić, but most commonly in the **east**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pine forests in the north and just north of Nikšić, but most common in the east.

clues.title: Landscape: grassy treeless high mountains
text: Durmitor National Park can be recognized by a distinct landscape consisting of **grassy, treeless mountains** with a high-altitude feel.

The town of [Žabljak](https://goo.gl/maps/ityFp93bD3WQweCq5) is situated in this national park, and can be recognized by the landscape but also by the [unique](https://goo.gl/maps/1dyUEW1YaCgDS1SU9) [architecture](https://goo.gl/maps/wQFbfwF88LLTbie77).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A national park with grassy, treeless mountains and a high-altitude feel. The town inside it has unusual architecture.

clues.title: City: modern buildings, wide roads
text: Podgorica is the capital and **largest city** in Montenegro, and can be recognized by the modern buildings, wide roads and modern infrastructure.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The capital and biggest city looks modern, with new buildings, wide roads and modern infrastructure.

clues.title: Landscape: staircase-like mountainsides
text: These distinct **staircase-like** mountainsides can be seen in the Cemi River Valley.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Mountainsides that look like steps, seen in the Cemi River valley.

clues.title: Landscape: lake with many small islands
text: Many small islands can be seen within **Slansko Lake**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A lake dotted with many small islands (Slansko Lake).

clues.title: Landmark: coal mine with gravel wall
text: The Pljevlja Coal Mine can be recognized by the wide, artificial **wall of gravel**. The mine can often be seen from [afar](https://goo.gl/maps/45CwG7nnsD9NjzXE6).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A coal mine recognisable by a wide, artificial wall of gravel, often visible from far away.

clues.title: Bollard: stone posts beside a railway bridge
text: The Skadar Lake Bridge can be recognized by the **railway** and stone bollards next to the road.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The Skadar Lake bridge has a railway next to the road and stone bollards along it.

The font is much thicker on speed signs in Albania.

clues.title: Language: Latin letters with Ś and Ź
text: Montenegrin is a South Slavic language and the only version of Serbo-Croatian official in Montenegro. However, Serbian is technically the most widely spoken language in Montenegro, ahead of Montenegrin. For the purpose of this map, these two languages might aswell be the same (they are **that** similar). Both Montenegrin and Serbian are officially written either in Latin or Cyrillic, but Latin is by far the more common script used in Montenegro. Road signs are **not** required to use both scripts, only Latin. Montenegrin uses the letters **Ś** and **Ź** which can not be found in Croatian/Bosnian/Serbian.
The Serbo-Croatian word for street is **ulica**/**улица** (like most Slavic languages).

images.caption: Montenegrin text with Ś and Ź shown large
Blue street sign with ulica in Cyrillic and Latin script

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A South Slavic language, nearly identical to Serbian. Mostly Latin script on signs. The letters Ś and Ź do not exist in Croatian, Bosnian or Serbian. Street is 'ulica'.
